deckTitle: Shadow Monopoly: The Great Octopus Wrestling Match — BlackRock, Vanguard & Co

cards.power: Play this card to completely ignore the rules of the base game.
cards.lore: The illusion of choice is a carefully constructed farce. Welcome to the Geopolitical Shadow Monopoly.
cards.gradeReason: Meta-card explains rather than invites. 'Welcome to' is orientation, not performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink collage. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit presenting expansion scroll to audience. Mood: anarchic welcome.

cards.power: Bind 4 of your opponent's cards. They belong to you now.
cards.lore: A single hidden head controlling economic tentacles gripping the globe. Less than a handful of mega-corporations own your morning coffee and your digital soul.
cards.gradeReason: Concept card — binding power is strong but the name is explanatory, not embodiment-first.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Giant octopus gripping globe with dollar-sign tentacles. Mood: quietly ominous.

cards.power: Epistemic Sabotage! Shuffle the discard pile into the government's tax returns.
cards.lore: The solo host of the deep dive. Armed with a sketchbook, cut-and-paste logic, and absolute layout anarchy.
cards.gradeReason: Host character with scissors and chaos energy — embodiment instant. 'Epistemic Sabotage' is G1 gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink collage. Subject: Rabbit with scissors and sketchbook amid cut newspaper fragments. Mood: irreverent anarchy.

cards.power: Drain $20 Trillion from the board by 2028.
cards.lore: The ultimate consolidating pyramidal network. All profits flow upward to the 0.01%.
cards.gradeReason: Power action lands hard but 'Power Plumbing' is structural, not an animal you can embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Pyramid of pipes draining upward into single elite vault. Mood: cold extraction.

cards.power: Coordinated Duopoly. If your opponent plays Sugar Water Blue, neither of you attack. Both players just extract profit from the source.
cards.lore: You think it's a cola war? Vanguard, BlackRock, and State Street own the top shares of both. It's brand theater while the profits flow to the exact same owners.
cards.gradeReason: Cola wars as bear duopoly is instant. Players perform 'coordinated brand theater' without prompting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Subject: Crimson bear clutching Coke can while winking at azure hound. Mood: conspiratorial cheerfulness.

cards.power: Market Homogenization. Double your immunity. Ignore all price-drop damage.
cards.lore: 73% owned by institutional investors. They don't fight for market share. The same financial firewall against real disruption.
cards.gradeReason: The brand-animal pairing makes the cola duopoly legible immediately. Twin-villain table energy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Subject: Azure hound lapping Pepsi can, winking at crimson bear. Mood: cheerful-sinister.

cards.power: Absorb all independent food brands on the table. Gain +10 Girth.
cards.lore: Unilever, Mondelez, Nestlé. You own every brand in your pantry. Competition in the food aisle is a carefully engineered stage play.
cards.gradeReason: +10 Girth. Trough equals feed trough equals engineered overconsumption. Players wallow in it immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Collage. Subject: Gleaming trough surrounded by 50 brand logos. Mood: excess and saturation.

cards.power: Patent the dirt. Opponents must pay you 1 token per turn just to keep their cards alive.
cards.lore: They own 90% of the world's cotton seed. They control the raw materials, the distribution, and the soil itself. Vertical integration from dirt to retail.
cards.gradeReason: 'Patent the dirt' is three words that contain the entire conspiracy. Locust eating seed = instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Locust devouring farmland with patent stamps as legs. Mood: predatory corporate hunger.

cards.power: Algorithmic Enclosure. Look at your opponent's hand and sell the information to the highest bidder.
cards.lore: Over 80% owned by institutional investors. It's not a social square; it's a data-extraction farm owned by the exact same firms dominating the food industry.
cards.gradeReason: Iguana surveillance stare plus 'sell to the highest bidder' — players are ON IT before you finish reading.
cards.artworkPrompt: Digital ink. Subject: Iguana with camera eyes scanning phone screens for data. Mood: cold silicon surveillance.

cards.power: Search Monopoly. You decide which cards your opponent is allowed to find in their deck.
cards.lore: They run the operating systems and the servers. The algorithm that feeds you the snacks controls the culture that runs your life.
cards.gradeReason: Owl deciding what you can find = knowledge god = instant. Decides your opponent's reality with a stare.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Owl in server room controlling search results on vast monitor wall. Mood: omniscient quiet.

cards.power: Walled Garden. No external cards can affect this entity.
cards.lore: The ultimate premium enclosure. Owned by the Big Four. A glittering cage built to keep alternative ecosystems from ever rising up.
cards.gradeReason: Snake in Garden of Eden with Apple device = richest image in the deck. Immediate embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Serpent coiled around bitten Apple device in walled digital garden. Mood: seductive-sinister.

cards.power: Forced Update. Your opponent skips a turn while their deck restarts.
cards.lore: From operating systems to cloud infrastructure, the backend of the world is just another asset in the institutional portfolio.
cards.gradeReason: Power is great. Moth metaphor is softer — flutters toward institutional money but doesn't bite like the others.
cards.artworkPrompt: Digital ink. Subject: Moth with blue-screen wings mid-forced update cycle. Mood: bureaucratic.

cards.power: Gentrification Strike. Replace an opponent's property card with an overpriced short-term rental.
cards.lore: Booking.com or Airbnb — doesn't matter. The same handful of financial entities form the economic foundation of your lodging.
cards.gradeReason: Bedbug-as-Airbnb is the pun of the decade. Gentrification Strike tells you exactly how to play it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Subject: Cheerful bedbug in tiny gentrified apartment with 5-star rating. Mood: sardonic hospitality.

cards.power: Surge Pricing. Double the cost of all actions this turn.
cards.lore: You think you're hunting for a deal? Expedia and Skyscanner are ultimately minor holdings of the exact same institutional groups.
cards.gradeReason: Hawk doubles costs = price predation made animal. Surge Pricing is the most hated retail mechanic — players feel it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Hawk circling with phone displaying tripling flight prices. Mood: predatory.

cards.power: Regulatory Capture. Ignore all safety checks. If you roll a 1, discard your hand in a fiery accident.
cards.lore: Boeing or Airbus? Doesn't matter — their largest shareholders are overlapping investment funds. They own the skies.
cards.gradeReason: Albatross = ancient curse + regulatory capture + fiery crash. Three registers, zero ambiguity. G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Albatross draped around burning aircraft nose, ignoring safety checklist. Mood: tragic-absurd.

cards.power: Astroturf. Create 5 fake review tokens to overwhelm the board.
cards.lore: The feedback loop is managed. The same owners control the planes, the beds, and the platform where you complain about them.
cards.gradeReason: Astroturf is perfect — but toad is just a toad. Needed more bite to hit G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Subject: Toad furiously generating fake five-star review tokens. Mood: slippery and self-satisfied.

cards.power: Primary Extraction. Take resources directly from your opponent's reserves before their turn starts.
cards.lore: The jet fuel for the planes comes from their oil companies. The monopoly extends backward into the raw earth itself.
cards.gradeReason: Squid with oil-derrick tentacles taking before your turn = extraction capitalism in animal form. Instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Squid with oil-derrick tentacles draining opponent's reserve wells. Mood: industrial-dark.

cards.power: Strip Mine. Destroy one of your own cards to draw three new ones.
cards.lore: The steel for the aircraft comes from their mining companies. They are the largest shareholders in the world's raw materials.
cards.gradeReason: Mole strips mine to draw more cards = sacrifice and extraction. Ecological and mechanical synergy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Mole operating strip-mine machinery, earth collapsing around it. Mood: underground extraction.

cards.power: Fast Fashion Web. Snare an opponent in cheap goods. They skip a turn.
cards.lore: From the cotton seeds to the sweatshops to the department stores. It's a vertically integrated web of unprecedented scale.
cards.gradeReason: Tarantula weaving sweatshops into web = vertical integration as spider = instant, beautiful, vicious.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Tarantula spinning cotton mill into web connecting cotton fields to department stores. Mood: industrial.

cards.power: Chronic Dependency. Opponent must pay you 1 token per turn just to keep their cards alive.
cards.lore: The institutional families own the largest global pharmaceutical companies. They don't want you cured; they want you subscribing.
cards.gradeReason: Viper venom = chronic dependency = subscription model. 'They want you subscribing' = verbal knockout.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Viper with pill-capsule fangs dripping subscription contract. Mood: predatory pharmaceutical.

cards.power: The Fourth Arm. In Architects Daughter: Override a government card. You 'are' the government now.
cards.lore: Managing trillions, advising central banks, and writing the financial software the world runs on. The undisputed titan of the pyramid.
cards.gradeReason: Vulture IS the government — four words, full conspiracy thesis. Strongest institutional card in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Vulture in suit at government podium with BlackRock letterhead. Mood: imperious and unfazed.

cards.power: Absolute Opacity. In Architects Daughter: Gain +5 share of BlackRock itself. The ultimate self-reinforcing monopoly loop.
cards.lore: A mutual company shell masking the true owners. They hold the largest share of BlackRock itself. The ultimate self-reinforcing monopoly loop.
cards.gradeReason: Kraken of opacity owning the vulture = Lovecraftian monopoly. Nobody sees it coming from the deep.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Kraken in deep water with BlackRock share certificates as tentacle rings. Mood: abyssal opacity.

cards.power: The Bronze Medal. In Architects Daughter: Gain +5 share as you stay out of the spotlight.
cards.lore: The quiet third pillar of the Big Three. Always present in the top shareholder lists, silently extracting wealth.
cards.gradeReason: Bronze Medal is funny but the quiet third-pillar role needs explaining. Wolf in shadow = G2.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Wolf in shadow near New York Stock Exchange, watching without being watched. Mood: quiet menace.

cards.power: Compound Interest. In Architects Daughter: Double this card's power every 2 turns.
cards.lore: The old-school holding company giant. A massive piece of the interlocking duopoly puzzle, holding hands with the new tech whales.
cards.gradeReason: Compound Interest doubling is mechanically sharp. Boar is earthy but less immediately embodiable than vulture or kraken.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Subject: Rotund boar with compound-interest abacus and folksy hat. Mood: folksy-sinister.

cards.power: Unfettered Access. Peek at the top 3 cards of the deck and rearrange them.
cards.lore: The public face of consolidated finance. He doesn't just meet with heads of state; he hands them their to-do lists.
cards.gradeReason: 'He hands them their to-do lists.' Plus Fink = fink = informant + bird of prey. Triple-layer G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Bird-creature in suit handing to-do list to suited world leaders. Mood: unelected power.

cards.power: Job Swap. Swap one of your cards on the board with one from your discard pile.
cards.lore: Former executives move into the White House; former politicians move to corporate boards. The line between private power and the state is a fiction.
cards.gradeReason: Revolving door = hamster wheel = the loop is closed. Mechanically and conceptually perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Subject: Giant hamster wheel spinning with Goldman Sachs suits and White House staffers. Mood: absurd.

cards.power: System Administrator. Change the rules of the current turn.
cards.lore: They didn't just lend money to the central banks; they built the computer system (Aladdin) that the central banks use to manage their finances.
cards.gradeReason: System Administrator power is vivid. Aladdin software reference is niche — works for insiders, G2 for everyone else.
cards.artworkPrompt: Digital ink. Subject: Chameleon blending into central bank supercomputer terminal named ALADDIN. Mood: invisible control.

cards.power: Continental Debt. Force an opponent to pay for your next card.
cards.lore: BlackRock acts as the European central banking system. Sovereign nations take orders from the corporate board.
cards.gradeReason: Bat-as-blood-drainer is good. 'Continental Debt' is mechanical. German context needs a beat to land fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Bat in European Parliament chamber draining sovereign funds with credit-card wings. Mood: nocturnal control.

cards.power: Financial Maneuvering. Protect all your assets from game penalties.
cards.lore: Non-profits are ideal vehicles for moving immense sums of money from unseen investors into areas of social and political influence. No taxes, no transparency.
cards.gradeReason: Vault as entity is structural rather than animal-embodied. Good power, but descriptive not performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Collage. Subject: Glowing vault floating above tax forms with invisible money arrows circling it. Mood: smug immunity.

cards.power: Global Health Czar. Control all healing and medical cards on the board.
cards.lore: When the US cut funding, he becomes the largest funder of the WHO. He funds the health bodies while partnering with the pharma companies. The loop is closed.
cards.gradeReason: 'The loop is closed' + control all healing cards = if you know the Gates story you become the hyena instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Hyena clutching syringe, laughing behind WHO podium with pharma logo backdrop. Mood: manic predatory.

cards.power: Funding the Narrative. Spawn 3 Activism tokens to block opponent's moves.
cards.lore: Moving billions to progressive reporting, fund local journalism centers, and shape global political shifts from the shadow.
cards.gradeReason: Owl = wisdom from shadow. Activism tokens are good. The Soros conspiracy is layered enough to need unpacking.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Owl funding protest banners from shadowed perch with money trail to newsrooms. Mood: strategic.

cards.power: Pandemic Declaration. Freeze the game board for one turn.
cards.lore: The global health authority. Who dictates their policy? Whoever drops the most coins in the slot.
cards.gradeReason: Piggybank = whoever drops coins controls output. Freeze the board = Pandemic Declaration. Instant and devastating.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Subject: Piggybank with WHO logo and donor slot on globe-shaped stand. Mood: absurd-sinister.

cards.power: Manufactured Consent. Opponent must agree with whatever you say this turn.
cards.lore: Disney, AT&T, Comcast. 90% of international media is owned by 9 conglomerates. The largest shareholders? Vanguard and BlackRock.
cards.gradeReason: Mouse-trap with Disney ears = best visual pun in the deck. Manufactured Consent as a power name = direct Chomsky hit.
cards.artworkPrompt: Collage. Subject: Mousetrap with Mickey ears snapping shut on media titles. Mood: manufactured and inevitable.

cards.power: The Raw Feed. Determine the starting conditions for the next round.
cards.lore: Local news doesn't investigate; they just print the centralized feed. The wire services are the root code of the global narrative.
cards.gradeReason: Pecking single narrative into newsprint is apt. Woodpecker is less immediately loaded than mouse-trap or ferret though.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Woodpecker hammering single wire-service headline into 156 newspapers simultaneously. Mood: repetitive centralization.

cards.power: Synchronized News. All players must play the same color card this turn.
cards.lore: Supplying the analytical slant for 156 countries. Funded by elite foundations to ensure a single, unified narrative dominates the globe.
cards.gradeReason: Spider web connecting 156 countries into single synchronized press. Forces table-wide compliance. Elegant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Spider with web spanning 156 newspaper mastheads in synchronized formation. Mood: centralized narrative.

cards.power: Information Scrub. Remove one of your opponent's cards from the game entirely. "It never existed."
cards.lore: Funded by the same conglomerates and foundations. Their job isn't journalism; it's ensuring no alternative perspectives survive.
cards.gradeReason: 'It never existed.' That's the whole card. Ferret sniffs out and buries. Perfect investigative irony.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Smug ferret stamping CENSORED on opponent's card with practiced efficiency. Mood: gleefully oppressive.

cards.power: High-Level Dealmaking. Trade your worst card for your opponent's 5 best cards.
cards.lore: Where CEOs, politicians, and media elites meet. They claim to solve global problems, but 71% of their budget comes from corporate partners buying access.
cards.gradeReason: Goat atop the mountain doing high-altitude deals. Trade worst for their 5 best is ruthless and embodiable instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Subject: Suited goat atop Davos peak surrounded by CEO heads looking upward. Mood: elevated contempt.

cards.power: The Great Reset. Wipe the entire board clean. All players start from zero.
cards.lore: "The pandemic represents a rare but narrow window of opportunity to reflect, reimagine, and reset our world." The grand architect of the new normal.
cards.gradeReason: Mole-rat blind underground reset architect = conceptually genius. Wiping the board is the most theatrical power in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Mole-rat with Great Reset blueprint unrolling in underground WEF bunker. Mood: subterranean mastermind.

cards.power: Conditional Rebuilding. Rebuild a destroyed card, but it now belongs to the State.
cards.lore: The synchronized motto chanted by globalist politicians worldwide. A promise to reconstruct society under a centralized, technocratic grid.
cards.gradeReason: Beaver rebuilds — but it belongs to the State now. Alliteration + animal + sting in the tail = pure G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Subject: Beaver reconstructing dam with STATE PROPERTY sign replacing old planks. Mood: chirpy-sinister.

cards.power: Joyful Servitude. Surrender your hand to your controller. The State's Happiness token.
cards.lore: "You will own nothing, and you will be happy." The ultimate promise of the WEF agenda. Conditional compliance for basic necessities.
cards.gradeReason: Sheeple smiling as they surrender cards = Joyful Servitude. WEF quote in lore = whole conspiracy in one sentence.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Subject: Smiling sheep handing full card hand to uniformed state shepherd. Mood: compliant bliss.

cards.power: [Partially legible — power text obscured by large illustration in source PDF. Appears to reference predictive pandemic simulation mechanics.]
cards.lore: [Partially legible — refers to October 2019 Johns Hopkins/Gates Foundation pandemic simulation.]
cards.gradeReason: Power concept is G1 but lore text is partially obscured in source PDF. Holding at G2 pending clean read.
cards.artworkPrompt: Collage. Subject: Suited figures at pandemic simulation table with bat overhead and 2019 calendar. Mood: predictive dread.

cards.power: Media Omnipresence. Speak with total unity. Opponent cannot play Alternative Voice cards.
cards.lore: Belgian virologist admitted on tape to strategically manipulating fear and mortality rates to encourage mass vaccine compliance.
cards.gradeReason: No animal form makes embodiment harder. Media Omnipresence is strong but card needs a creature to hit G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Wolf-in-suit at press conference surrounded by unified camera wall. Mood: manufactured fear.

cards.power: Predictive Origin. Play this card 5 turns in advance. When triggered, it causes massive Board damage.
cards.lore: The German Robert Koch Institute ran a 2012 simulation of a coronavirus jumping from an animal in a Southeast Asian market. A perfect dress rehearsal.
cards.gradeReason: Bat = COVID vector + Koch = German bureaucrat bat = play 5 turns in advance = prophecy mechanic is pure theater.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: German bat emerging from Koch Institute lab into Southeast Asian wet market. Mood: ominous origin.

cards.power: Manufactured Demand. Make one of your low-value cards an irresistibly expensive must-have to opponent.
cards.lore: Van Ranst leveraged the desire of professional soccer players to get the vaccine first to artificially pressure public demand. Fear is the ultimate marketing tool.
cards.gradeReason: Manufactured Demand is sharp but the footballer-as-vaccine-marketing-tool requires the backstory to perform fully.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Footballer receiving golden syringe at stadium press event, cameras flashing. Mood: manufactured prestige.

cards.power: [Partially legible — power text obscured by large illustration in source PDF.]
cards.lore: [Partially legible — power text obscured by large illustration in source PDF.]
cards.gradeReason: Trojan horse is one of civilization's oldest performance archetypes. The name alone is G1 — text is bonus.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Blue UN-branded Trojan horse with globalist octopus emerging from hidden chamber. Mood: deceptive.

cards.power: Sky is Falling. All players must discard their resources to save the board.
cards.lore: Crises are viewed as opportunities. Climate panic is leveraged to justify the massive transfer of wealth and the dismantling of the old normally.
cards.gradeReason: 'Sky is Falling' + chicken = the fable turned into a devastating power mechanic. Immediate, classic, perfect.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Subject: Panicked chicken with flaming sky overhead pointing up at burning atmosphere. Mood: apocalyptic comedy.

cards.power: Full Tracking. You can see your opponent's cards for the rest of the game.
cards.lore: State of 2030 ostensibly aims to end poverty and hunger. The fine print? Citizens must surrender fundamental rights and will to achieve it.
cards.gradeReason: Collar = you're owned. Full Tracking for rest of game = persistent surveillance. Embodiment is physical and immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Digital ink. Subject: Dog with QR-code collar being scanned for entry through digital checkpoint. Mood: surveilled.

cards.power: Sovereignty Surrender. Remove all border mechanics from the game. You rule the entire board.
cards.lore: The underlying principle of the Great Reset: nations must surrender sovereignty to an all-encompassing governing body to manage the transition.
cards.gradeReason: Leviathan = Hobbes' total state = rule the entire board. Four centuries of political theory in one card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Leviathan rising from sea to consume sovereign border checkpoints. Mood: total governance.

cards.power: Forced Debt. Opponent must borrow tokens from you at 200% interest.
cards.lore: Step 1: A concerted attack on the middle class. Force small entrepreneurs into debt, leading to massive asset loss and dependency.
cards.gradeReason: Nutcracker cracking the middle class = immediate visceral metaphor. 200% interest is the crunch made mechanical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Nutcracker in banker suit clamping down on small business card at 200% interest. Mood: mechanical.

cards.power: System Failure. Erase all saved tokens on the board.
cards.lore: Step 2: Engineer a widespread bank collapse. When the system crashes, the whales swallow the remains of the small fish.
cards.gradeReason: Bear market bear is apt. The 'Step 2' framing makes it documentary rather than performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Bear market grizzly scooping small fish savings from collapsed bank vault. Mood: institutional predation.

cards.power: Digital Transition. All physical cash cards become worthless. Play only with abstract points.
cards.lore: Step 3: The elimination of physical Moving entirely to programmable digital currencies controlled exclusively by central banks.
cards.gradeReason: Bonfire of physical cash with digital QR rising from the ashes = instant visual and tactile performance trigger.
cards.artworkPrompt: Collage. Subject: Pile of banknotes burning with CBDC QR code rising from flames. Mood: celebratory-ominous.

cards.power: Conditional Support. Opponent gives you all their properties in exchange for 1 Survival Ration.
cards.lore: Step 4: Making state support conditional on the complete relinquishing of private property. You will own nothing.
cards.gradeReason: Vacuum sucking assets is clear. The 'Step 4' framing again makes it feel like a diagram not a performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Industrial vacuum inhaling houses, cars, savings upward into state repository. Mood: irresistible force.

cards.power: Infinite Power. Draw cards until your hand is full, without paying costs.
cards.lore: Nikola Tesla's fundamental discoveries into clean, free energy systems were an existential threat to the centralized power grid monopoly. Shut down and suppressed.
cards.gradeReason: Tesla's pigeon obsession is historical fact. Free energy as infinite hand-drawing = suppressed potential finally released.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Glowing pigeon transmitting free energy from Tesla tower, cards flowing endlessly to hand. Mood: suppressed wonder.

cards.power: Radio Healing. Remove all poison and damage from your deck instantly.
cards.lore: Dr. Rife allegedly used specific radio frequencies to heal cancer. A direct threat to the trillion-dollar pharmaceutical dependency model. He died under suspicious circumstances.
cards.gradeReason: Radio-frequency bat sonar is clever. Rife is obscure enough that lore is load-bearing — G2 for now.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Bat emitting radio-wave sonar healing beams, pharma logos dissolving. Mood: hopeful-suppressed.

cards.power: Bio-Armor. This card cannot be destroyed by conventional attacks.
cards.lore: Henry Ford's experimental 1941 car made of bioplastic was stronger than steel. Suppressed because it threatened the petrochemical and raw material monopolies.
cards.gradeReason: Armored hemp-car tortoise = unstoppable slow alternative. Bio-Armor is the mechanic AND the material. Vivid.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Subject: Tortoise with hemp-car shell plating, impervious to oil-industry weapons. Mood: resilient.

cards.power: Public Unity. Combine the power of all your cards. The Line's greatest feat.
cards.lore: A truly free, sustainable world without chronic pollution and manufactured poverty is entirely possible. It starts with recognizing the structure and breaking the dependency.
cards.gradeReason: Bear rises with unified crowd energy. Combines all cards = the table rallies. Perfect investigative deck finale.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Massive bear rising with unified crowd card energy flowing upward. Mood: triumphant awakening.

cards.power: Do Your Own Research. Search the entire deck for any one card.
cards.lore: JFK warned of a monolithic and ruthless conspiracy relying on infiltration. Instead of invasion. It's not a theory; it's a documented, interlocking corporate fact.
cards.gradeReason: Tinfoil hat fox doing DYOR = self-aware conspiracy comedy + genuine research power. Players love playing the Fox.
cards.artworkPrompt: Watercolor. Subject: Fox with tin-foil hat searching archive filing cabinet for single truth card. Mood: righteous paranoia.

cards.power: Inherited Monopoly. Start the game with half the board already under your control.
cards.lore: Who owns Vanguard? The wealthiest families hiding behind corporate shells for generations. The apex of the banking system.
cards.gradeReason: Bloodline dragon = ancient inherited power = start with half the board. Peak conspiracy card. Immediately theatrical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Ancient dragon atop generational pile of corporate shell company papers. Mood: dynastic cold.

cards.power: The Unexplained. Force an opponent to skip their turn out of sheer bewilderment.
cards.lore: The true, fundamental motives relate to history beyond rational thinking. How do they maintain control over their underlings? Institutional blackmail methods.
cards.gradeReason: Vault as leverage-keeper is structural. 'Sheer bewilderment' is FrizzleBob-level irony but vault doesn't embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Ink. Subject: Sealed vault with tendrils of unknown leverage reaching toward suited figures. Mood: occluded.

cards.power: Cut & Play. Physically cut an opponent's card in half (or just pretend to, for legal reasons). You win.
cards.lore: The power to choose rests entirely with you. Stay skeptical, stay sharp, and keep seeking the truth behind the curtain. Peace out.
cards.gradeReason: Deck closes with scissors that end everything. 'Or just pretend to, for legal reasons' = peak FrizzleBob sign-off.
cards.artworkPrompt: Collage. Subject: Giant scissors cutting Monopoly board in half, FrizzleBob waving behind cut edge. Mood: liberating finale.

verdict: The Great Octopus is the deck FrizzleBob was born to curate — 60 animal metaphors each embodying a different tentacle of the same shadow monopoly. Named strength: the creature-naming system is architecturally consistent from THE CRIMSON COLA BEAR all the way down to THE BLACKMAIL VAULT; every animal does exactly what it says. Named weakness: the Step 1/2/3/4 framing on the Pathway to Owning Nothing spread slips into documentary mode, breaking the performance invitation. Two cards have partially obscured text in the source PDF (Event 201 power, U.N. Trojan Horse). Table-ready: Yes.
blurb: 60 corporate predator cards where BlackRock is a vulture, Vanguard is a kraken, and the Great Reset is a mole-rat. For anyone who's ever wondered who owns the owners.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — Octopus gripping globe with dollar tentacles plus FrizzleBob scissors iconography = iconic, immediately shareable
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'THE GREAT OCTOPUS WRESTLING MATCH! / Bow to your new corporate overlords!' is a perfect hook
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Conspiracy-investigative satire tone nailed on first glance
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — Animal-as-corporation naming is highly original; shadow-monopoly theme itself is familiar in conspiracy media
coverQA.coverViral: 5 — 'BlackRock Vulture' and 'Vanguard Kraken' alone will get the deck screenshot-shared
coverQA.coverNote: This cover does exactly what FrizzleBob's scissors promise: cuts through the noise. The central octopus-gripping-globe image with the cut-out instruction tagline is better than 80% of what's on the deck market. One watch-out: cut instructions on the cover reduce first-impression impact for digital viewers — move to inside page for web version.

notes: Font annotations 'Architects Daughter' appear as floating text labels on cards in pages 7, 10, and 11 — approximately 9 instances total, clearly unremoved designer labels. The 'Luckiest Guy' page-section headers (pages 10-14) appear intentional as thematic labels and are NOT counted as artifacts. Two cards have obscured text due to large illustrations dominating the card area: EVENT 201 (p11 TL) and THE U.N. TROJAN HORSE (p12 TL). Page 6 uses a horizontal single-row layout (4 wide cards) rather than standard 2x2 grid. All 15 pages are landscape format 745x415pt with one full-page image per page. The Step 1/2/3/4 framing on page 13's Pathway spread is the only area where investigative mode slips into documentary mode.

Kayfabizarro: SHADOW MONOPOLY – Who Owns the Owners? (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Who owns the owners?

You think the brands compete. Pepsi against Coke, Disney against the world, your bank against the bank across the street. Pull the ownership thread on any of them and the same three asset managers turn up at the top of the cap table, voting both corners of every fight. This deck draws them as what they are: BlackRock a vulture, Vanguard a kraken, the Great Reset a blind mole-rat digging under the floor you are standing on.

This is wrestling for the ownership question. Sixty cut-and-play cards turn the Big Three and the industries they quietly hold into a bestiary you can pick up, perform, and pin. You take a predator, you run its move out loud with a straight face, and the table rules whether the racket holds or gets exposed mid-sentence. Social Story Wrestling for anyone who ever followed a logo upstream and found the same parent waiting at the end.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Shadow Monopoly Core Deck: 60 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring THE BLACKROCK VULTURE, THE DISNEY-VIACOM MOUSE-TRAP, and THE DOOMSDAY CHICKEN.
- The Freestyle Rules: The complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, no finance degree, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the one law that every card can claim anything, as long as you can sell the claim before the room calls the bluff.
- The Predator Bestiary: the whole apparatus racked as creatures you trigger on purpose, from EVENT 201 to THE U.N. TROJAN HORSE, so you stop reading about concentrated ownership and start running it across a table.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
By grabbing this deck, you aren't just buying a static PDF. You are entering the Protopian Pipeline. All future thematic expansions and topic-specific decks in this cycle are included as FREE updates for you.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I make these because the ownership map is public record that almost nobody actually reads, and a deck you play beats a chart you scroll past. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Play it. Trace the cap table in your own head. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the next cards and the next match.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"The octopus has no face. Draw one, and you can finally pin it."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
